sports.label: Golf
sports.official_register_note: PGA Tour schedule confirms the 2026 season; LPGA.com confirms the Maybank Championship (29 Oct-1 Nov, Kuala Lumpur G&CC, $3m purse). Only three outright tournament markets currently carry OLBG tips; no match-bet or 2/3-ball markets were listed at capture.

rows.competition: LPGA Tour, Kuala Lumpur G&CC West Course
flags: LPGA field includes world Nos 3-10: Ryu, Yamashita, Yin, Woad (No.7), Hull (No.8), Green (No.10) per LPGA entry list and field reports
FanDuel market leaders: Yamashita +480, Yin +650, Ryu +850; Woad around 28/1 in oddschecker snapshot
Outright fields are high-variance; confidence low even for the favourite
rows.prediction: Lottie Woad each-way/back to win the Maybank Championship, treated as a low-confidence outright. The LPGA entry list confirms a stacked Kuala Lumpur field with six of the world's top ten including Haeran Ryu, Miyu Yamashita and Ruoning Yin, while Woad arrives as world No.7 and a winner on tour this season at the Kroger Queen City. Market leaders sit around +480 to +850 and Woad is a 28/1 chance, so the edge is small; selection: Woad in the win tournament market, staked as an outright flyer rather than a strong play.

flags: Media odds (Golf Channel/Hard Rock Bet/DraftKings, 26 Oct): Clark +1000 to +1125 favourite; Tom Kim +1750; Ben James +1850/+2000
$6m purse, 120-player field, 500 FedExCup points; Clark has three PGA Tour wins this season
rows.prediction: Wyndham Clark to win the Mexico Open at Vidanta Vallarta, a low-confidence outright on a 120-player field. Multiple bookmakers make Clark the market favourite at about +1000 to +1125 after three PGA Tour wins this season, and OLBG's sole recorded tournament tip agrees. Tom Kim and Ben James head the chasing pack in the betting. Selection: Clark in the win tournament market; with even the favourite implied below ten percent, this is an each-way-style flyer, not a high-confidence play.

The OLBG card shows a two-tip split with Cink the recorded selection, and the veteran's length and putting remain well suited to the tour's regular venues. Without an extracted official field or market price this stays a low-confidence, small-stake outright. Selection: Cink to win the tournament, flagged as needing an official field check before staking.

sports.label: Darts
sports.official_register_note: PDC.tv news (26 Oct 2026) confirms Players Championships 31-32 at Maassport Den Bosch, Netherlands on 28-29 Oct and lists entries; PDC and specialist outlets report mass withdrawals including Littler, Humphries, Clayton, Price, Bunting, Anderson and Rock. The PDC tournaments page itself returned a cookie wall, so the news article is the cited official-adjacent source.

rows.competition: PDC Pro Tour floor event, Den Bosch
flags: OLBG's 25% Aspinall call is an underdog view in an open floor field
PDC confirms Aspinall entered; Littler, Humphries, Clayton, Price, Bunting, Anderson, Rock and others withdrew
Floor events are best-of-11 early rounds, high variance
rows.prediction: Nathan Aspinall each-way in Players Championship 31 in Den Bosch, a low-confidence outright on a depleted floor field. The PDC's own entry announcement confirms Aspinall is playing while Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Jonny Clayton, Gerwyn Price, Stephen Bunting and Gary Anderson are among the withdrawals, which thins the top of the draw considerably. Aspinall's major-match pedigree stands out in what remains, though two of eight OLBG tips is a minority view and best-of-11 floor darts is notoriously open. Selection: Aspinall to win the tournament, small stake.

flags: Reigning world champion; 61% of OLBG tips but two months remain before the draw
Ante-post only; no injury bulletin reviewed
rows.prediction: Luke Littler ante-post to retain the PDC World Championship. Twenty-two of thirty-six OLBG tips back the reigning champion, the clearest tournament consensus on the darts board, and his scoring ceiling remains the benchmark of the sport. The caveat is timing: the tournament does not begin until 3 January and a two-month stake tie-up plus a 96-player draw cap the confidence at medium. Selection: Littler in the win tournament market.

sports.label: Motor Racing
sports.official_register_note: Formula1.com official 2026 calendar confirms Round 19 Mexico City GP on 30 Oct-1 Nov and shows Kimi Antonelli dominating the season with multiple wins, explaining OLBG's 'Drivers Championship Without Antonelli' market. Only two OLBG motor-racing markets are currently active.

flags: Two-tip OLBG market; podium market pays on a top-three finish, lower variance than race winner
Verstappen has a strong Mexico City record historically; no 2026-specific team form extracted beyond the official calendar
rows.prediction: Selection: Max Verstappen - Yes for a podium finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The official F1 calendar confirms Round 19 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez next weekend, and a top-three finish is a far more forgiving target than a race win in a season where Mercedes have taken most victories. Verstappen's record at altitude in Mexico and the Red Bull package's straight-line strength make the podium a realistic floor. Selection: Verstappen podium - yes, medium confidence.

rows.event: Formula 1 Drivers Championship 2026 - Without Kimi Antonelli
flags: Market removes the runaway championship leader Antonelli, per the official 2026 results listing multiple Antonelli wins
Four of seven OLBG tips on Verstappen; two-horse race dynamics with Russell and others possible
rows.prediction: Max Verstappen in the Drivers Championship 'Without Kimi Antonelli' market. The official 2026 results page shows Antonelli winning repeatedly, which is precisely why this market excludes him; among the remaining runners Verstappen is the most consistent race-winning presence on the board and four of seven OLBG tips agree. Russell's Mercedes form is the main threat. Selection: Verstappen to head the Antonelli-excluded standings, medium confidence.

flags: Unanimous six-tip market; county club fixture absent from national GAA.ie extractor
+0.5 means the bet wins on an Eire Og win or draw
rows.prediction: Selection: Eire Og Cor +0.5 against Kanturk in the Cork club championship. All six OLBG tips take the half-point start, which means the selection wins with an Eire Og victory or a draw, and a comment is attached to the market. Eire Og's organised counter-attacking game is well suited to staying within a score against a Kanturk side that tends to dominate possession without always converting. Selection: Eire Og +0.5, medium confidence, with the county-level source gap flagged.

flags: County club fixture absent from national GAA.ie extractor
+3.5 wins unless Fr Caseys win by four points or more
rows.prediction: Selection: Kildimo Pallaskenry +3.5 against Fr Caseys. Five of seven OLBG tips take the underdog start, which keeps the bet alive unless Fr Caseys win by four or more. Club championship games of this type are frequently one-score affairs, and Kildimo's defensive structure is built to keep margins tight. Selection: Kildimo-Pallaskenry +3.5, medium confidence pending county-board confirmation of team news.

flags: OLBG notes Kerry hold the all-time record with 39 titles; Mayo are reigning champions after winning in 2026
Long-dated ante-post; low-medium confidence
rows.prediction: Kerry ante-post for the 2027 All-Ireland Football Championship. Six of eight OLBG tips back the Kingdom, who remain the most decorated county in the competition's history with 39 titles, though Mayo are the reigning champions after their 2026 success ended a long wait. Kerry's squad depth and underage pipeline support the bounce-back narrative. Selection: Kerry in the win tournament market, low-medium confidence given the nine-month horizon.

flags: 69% of OLBG tips on NSW; long-dated series market; medium confidence
rows.prediction: New South Wales in the 2027 State of Origin series. Nine of thirteen OLBG tips favour the Blues, the strongest consensus on the rugby-league card, and Origin betting tends to reward the side with the deeper selection pool once squad camps refine game plans. Seven months remain before kick-off, so coaching and injury news will move the price substantially. Selection: New South Wales to win the series, medium confidence.
